message: `effect(io, unsafe)` on `comma` names 2 effects, and an `effect(...)` tag names one
label: one effect per `effect(...)` tag
notes: a list here was read as ONE effect spelled with the comma in it, which nothing declares - so the claim could never be satisfied, and AX3010 reported it missing from a body that performed it. `restrict(...)` takes a comma list; `effect(...)` does not
help: write one tag line per effect: `;@axiom:effect(io)` and `;@axiom:effect(unsafe)`

message: `comma` performs IO and its declaration does not say so
notes: effects are INFERRED transitively, so this fires on every function up the call chain, and each one is a place a reader would otherwise have to open the callee to learn it. If the effect is not wanted here the fix is to stop performing it, not to stop saying so. `IO`, `Entropy`, `Spawn` and `Block` are required; `Alloc` and `Mut` are ambient and never need declaring

message: `comma` touches raw memory and its declaration does not say so
label: __load64
help: this fires where the unsafe operation is performed, not up the call chain. The tag makes the declaration a trusted encapsulation, whose callers inherit nothing. If the operation is not wanted here the fix is to stop performing it, not to stop saying so
